To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
redemption momentum exists, prior purchase behavior enhances redemption decisions, and redemption enhances future purchases.

the mere decision of an LP member to redeem a reward has a significant positive impact on the purchase behavior of that member, and that this impact is enhanced if the member has a history of prior purchases.
redemption of LP rewards significantly increases purchase behavior both before and after the reward is redeemed, and that this increase is independent of how much of the reward is redeemed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how members of a loyalty program choose to redeem rewards.
the effects of reward redemption on members' behavior, which is a key element of loyalty management.
the interplay between LP members' purchase and reward redemption behavior, which is an important topic for both researchers and practitioners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the redemption of LP rewards enhances the purchase behavior of LP members, even when members are not forced by point expiration to redeem.
the mere decision of a member to redeem his accumulated points has a positive impact on the member's future purchase behavior.

LPs should be designed to enhance the redemption of rewards, as this has an important impact not only on LP members' redemption behavior, but also on their purchase behavior before and even after the redemption event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LP managers should be aware that redemption is not only a mechanism to enhance members' behavior, but also a mechanism that is enhanced by members' behavior.
the mere act of redeeming rewards is a powerful marketing tool.
redemption momentum is an additional explanation for the existence of pre-reward effects in LPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mere decision of a member to redeem his/her accumulated points enhances his/her purchase behavior, which is an effect that is not well captured by the existing literature.
the mere act of redeeming a reward, even when members choose when to do so, can enhance purchase behavior.
LP managers need to understand that the decision to redeem a small amount of points can have a substantial impact on future purchase behavior.
